title: As a power user, my devices find the host on the local network and connect without an account or a vendor server in between
As a power user, I can reach my machine away from home, with the relay, VPN, or port-forward path documented
As a power user, a new device must be paired or explicitly approved before it can see or control the screen
As an IT admin, I can set up unattended access to a machine with credentials configured in advance, so no one has to sit at the host to accept
As a power user, the stream is hardware-encoded and low-latency enough for interactive work, not just passive viewing
As a power user, quality adapts when the link falls behind, and I can set resolution and frame rate myself
As a power user, I can view a specific monitor, window, or app on a multi-display host and switch between them mid-session
As a power user, mouse, keyboard, and scroll input from the viewing device lands on the host as native events
As a power user, touch and stylus input on a tablet or phone maps to pointer events on the host
As a power user, the clipboard moves both ways between host and viewer, and I can turn that off
As a power user, I can transfer files between the host and the viewing device inside a session
As a power user, a tablet or spare device works as an additional display that extends the desktop, not only a mirror of it
As a power user, the host can create a virtual display, so a streamed window keeps rendering when covered or the machine runs headless
As an IT admin, sessions are encrypted end to end with the protocol documented, not just asserted
As a power user, I can scope what a connected device may do: view only, control, clipboard, or file access
As a power user, the host shows who is connected right now, and I can disconnect or revoke a device from the host
As an IT admin, I can self-host the rendezvous or relay infrastructure so session traffic stays on infrastructure I run
As a power user, clients cover the desktop and mobile platforms I use, and host and viewer can run on different operating systems
As a power user, someone can view or control a session from a plain browser with nothing installed
As an IT admin, I can mass-deploy the client with preset configuration through MSI, MDM, or a documented silent install
As an IT admin, I can see a log of who connected to which machine and when, exportable for audit
As an IT admin, machines and users are organized in a shared address book or console with per-group access policies
